content.text: Now the Core Rules section A (HS-6, HS-10).

content.content:
171	**HS-5. Non-reading fields come from `Suit.view(player_id)`.** *Rule.* Allowed: the per-axis rungs and `vitals_state`, `locomotion_cap`, `equipped_slot`, tool charges, `glowstick_count`, `carried_def_id`, `beam_shape`, whether the cell exists (`CELL_ENABLED`), plus `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance` and `tool_charge`, **and the breath source `breath_src` (the Suit's enum 0 ROOM / 1 RESERVE / 2 GASP / 3 NONE; a `view()` field, not a reading)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `breath_src` is the HUD's one input for three presentation choices, and for nothing else: which of two readings the strip's breath dial shows (HS-12), whether the source-exists hue is O2 Cyan or Graphite lit (ROOM or RESERVE: Cyan; GASP or NONE: Graphite lit; HS-20, HSV-4), and whether the reserve cell's mark slot is also eligible (HS-22). It is a published enum, so the hue and the dial choice are frame-register decisions (class A, bit-identical with the Filter on or off, AC-HS-139) and not a corruptible reading; the HUD never derives a source from a `displayed_*` value. The four pre-wrap reading fields of `view()` (`o2_pp_dkpa`, `reserve_pm`, `cell_pm`, `integrity_pm`) are **never drawn**: a HUD that draws a number from them is a defect (the Suit's lint AC-SE-77). *Why.* A number drawn from `view()` would bypass the single wrap point (P4). *Edge notes.* In tests only, `view()` reading fields may be compared against the drawn value on the honest path (the second-instrument assertion, HS-14).
172	
173	**HS-6. The read interface is closed.** *Rule.* The HUD's reads are exactly those in the table below; anything else is a scope breach.
174	
175	| Read | Owner | Fields the HUD uses | Frequency | Never read |
176	|---|---|---|---|---|
177	| `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` x 5, plus the one-bit `perceived(SUIT_KEY(suit.alarm), PlayerId)` for the ship-alarm mark (a TRUTH key with its lie stage pinned `never`; how the one bit sits in the record is the Filter's, OQ-HS-8; **the Filter does not yet define the key, OQ-HS-79, so this read is provisional**) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Perception Filter | the record fields of HS-4 | every render frame | the true value, the lie id or kind as content |
178	| `perceived(SCANNER, PlayerId)` *(MVP-live and honest: Sanity SN-19, Interaction IA-30; only what a scan shows is provisional — ASK Sanity / Interaction)* | Perception Filter | same record | while the scanner slot is shown | — |
179	| `Suit.view(PlayerId)` + `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance`, `tool_charge` | Suit & Equipment | HS-5 list | discrete part: on dirty key `S/<PlayerId>`; forced rebuild list in HS-7 | the four reading fields |
180	| `focus_view(seat)` | Interaction | `focus_ref`, `anchor_o`, `verb_id`, `mode`, `duration_class`, `tool_required`, `prompt_state`, `verb_name_key`, `glyph_action`, `focus_seq`, and the fields Interaction's design review added (IA-41): `press_blocked_moving` (the HUD dims the plate one step, never hides it), `carry_state`, `drop_available`, `drop_anchor_o` (the second drop plate, HS-43; drawing details are the UX spec's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | every render frame | `interaction.state`, `node()`, `edge()`, any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block |
181	| `channel_view(seat)` (local seat only) | Interaction | `owner`, `verb_id`, `state`, `transition_seq`, `result_seq`, `progress_pm`, `length_class`, `outcome`, `ended_by` | every render frame | `abort_cause` (Interaction IA-41: "diagnostic only"; the cancel drain is keyed off the non-diagnostic `ended_by` instead, HS-41) |
182	| `confirm_view(seat)` *(the HUD's single named read for the hold and the press; the Controller publishes it as `confirm_view = {b, pressed, released}`, pci:953, and Interaction IA-41 names the same read `input_view(seat) = {hold_pm, armed, device_class, pressed_action}`, owned by the Controller; **the two names and field sets must be reconciled by the Controller (OQ-HS-18)**, this GDD uses `confirm_view` and the union below)* | Player Controller (Adapter-local, per render frame) | `{mode, hold_pm, armed, pressed_action, released}`: `mode` the Controller's `confirm_mode` (`HOLD` or `TAP`, pci:552 / 882); `hold_pm` 0..1000, the D.10 bar fill `b` as permille (the Controller drains it itself at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE`; the HUD draws it, `fill_px = (hold_pm * L) div 1000`, and does no drain of its own for a hold); `armed` the tap-confirm armed state; `pressed_action` the closed action token whose press is being acknowledged, or none; `released` true on the frame a held action is released. The Controller's published shape lacks `mode` and `armed` (Interaction's lacks `mode` and `released`): an ASK to add them (OQ-HS-18). **A Controller-side story (add `mode` and `armed` to `confirm_view`) explicitly blocks the HUD's TAP-mode relabel and armed-bracket story (HS-42)**; the ACK, hold-fill and glyph-swap stories depend only on the fields already published (`b`, `pressed`, `released`, `device`, `token`) and are not blocked | every render frame while a hold, a tap-arm or a press is live | — |
183	| `glyph_view(seat, action)` *(agreed in shape: pci:953)* | Player Controller (Adapter) | `{device, token}`: `device` in {KBM, PAD}, switched under `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS`; `token` from the Controller's **closed `keycap_token` enumeration** (one token per key, mouse button and gamepad button or axis direction its binding table can hold; a binding outside it fails the Controller's data-load lint). The `?` keycap (HS-37) is the HUD's fallback only for a token its own **atlas** lacks, never a member of the Controller's enumeration | on device switch | `InputEvent.device`, any comparison to `0` |
184	| The result-event record *(Interaction IA-41 source 4; agreed in shape)* | Interaction / kernel CR-5 projection | `{seat, command_id, queued_tick, kind}` with `kind` in {APPLIED, REJECTED, DROPPED, SUPERSEDED}, for the local seat's own commands only, carrying **no reason**; used to withdraw an ACK and to time the reject presentation | on each result | the reject reason |
185	| `save_status`, the fallback-load flag, `restore_reason` (a request only) | Save/Load | `IDLE / WRITING / WRITTEN / FAILED`; the consecutive-failure threshold is cited, not counted | on change | the failure count's meaning beyond the threshold |
186	| Committed tick `T`, `tick_alpha`, `present_time`, picture rect, `H`, `world_to_hud(pos)` | Kernel, Render Pipeline | as named | every render frame | the jolt offset; the world camera pose directly |
187	| O2 band edges | Life-Support Graph | `O2_BAND_ANOXIC_PP`, `HYPOXIA_PP`, `O2_BAND_THIN_PP` (registry; HS-13) | at load | any compartment state, `failures()`, `alarm_eligible` |
188	
189	The HUD never reads Attention, Horror, Sanity state, the Graph's state at a distance, `peer_id`, `lit(ref)` or the beam's exposure; `prompt_state` already carries what Interaction decided about lighting. *Why.* Reflexion pattern 11: list only what the consumer must supply, never a producer's internals; Graph UI item 4 forbids ship status at a distance; P3.
190	
191	**HS-7. Update model: hybrid pull.** *Rule.* Each render frame the HUD pulls the five `perceived` records, `focus_view(seat)`, `channel_view(seat)` and the Adapter reads of HS-6 (they can change every frame: glide, re-projection, bar). The seat's dirty key `S/<PlayerId>` and `save_status` changes decide only whether the **discrete** model (rungs, `vitals_state`, rail counts, `equipped_slot`, `carried_def_id`, the notice) is rebuilt. A rebuild is **forced** regardless of the key on: the first `RUNNING` frame, any restore, an `ALL`-coalesced notification (above `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256), exit from `PAUSED`, and any change of `H`, locale or glyph device. Notifications carry no state. *Why.* A coalesced `ALL` must not strand a stale reading; readings can glide so they must be pulled; the discrete rebuild is a dozen integer reads so the skip is a convenience, not a correctness dependency. -> ADR candidate C.
192	
193	**HS-8. Clocks.** *Rule.* Reading settle, prompt debounce, bar fill, bar drain, tick phases and lie motion advance on `present_time`, which is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`. The warning-mark phase is read from the committed kernel tick `T` and interpolated by `tick_alpha` (HS-23), **and so are the honest-numeral grid (`T mod HONEST_GRID_TICKS == 0`, HS-14) and the flash arbiter's window (`(T - TICK_RATE, T]`, HS-47)**, which freeze with `T` under pause; while `PAUSED` an active mark is held ON solid instead (HS-23), the one exception to the frozen-frame rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the grid moved from `present_time` to `T` so it cannot drift against the mark's own `T`-locked edges)* Layer 3 (the Chart Table) runs on process time. A time step fed to any presentation timer after a pause, a window-focus loss or a hitch is clamped (`HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` 50 `[PH]`), and no integrator divides by the time step. *Why.* The art bible 7.4 "the world simply stops"; the Pipeline's own state table says "HUD visible (frozen readings); chart table live on process time". The Pipeline's PR-9 prose "Layers 2-4 run on the engine's process time" is the stale clause (refresh owed: "Layers 3-4"; Cross-References). *Edge notes.* The Pipeline's PR-8 item 6 ("never on the tick counter") needs the matching wording refresh "never counts ticks; may read `T` and `tick_alpha` for clock-locked phases". -> ADR candidate B.
194	
195	**HS-9. Integer HUD-pixel placement and primitives, at every `H` and display.** *Rule (observable).* Every element is authored in HUD px (1 HUD px = `H` screen px), anchored to an edge or the centre of the HUD canvas `picture / H` (which may be fractional: the Deck's 1280 x 800 picture at `H` 3 is 426.67 wide), and snapped by `anchor_snap` so that every edge lands on a whole HUD px. Sizes are exact integer multiples of `H`. **Coordinate space (design review, 2026-10-27):** `HudLayout` outputs **integer HUD-px rectangles relative to the HUD-root `Control`** that the pipeline root sizes to `hud_rect / H` on every `RESCALING` (Pipeline PR-12, as amended; `world_to_hud` returns coordinates in the same space). The scale `H`, the sub-`H` screen-pixel remainder (`extra_x`) and any letterbox offset are carried by that Control's placement and the `CanvasLayer` transform, not by `HudLayout`; D.9's screen-pixel terms are the conversion a test uses, not a second layout space. **The default is manual snapping in `HudLayout`** (floor every rectangle to a whole HUD px and split the remainder as D.9 says); `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` is neither sourced nor relied on, and spikes S1 and S4 are **prerequisites of the layout / widget ADR**, not non-gating (the property, if it works, is a bonus). Layout and settings changes (`H`, locale, picture rect, `k_auto`) take effect on the **next render frame in every state, including `PAUSED_FROZEN`** (the layout is a pure function of `(picture rect, H)`; no simulation or presentation timer is advanced by it). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `Control.scale` is (1, 1) everywhere; no node animates scale or rotation; the 4.7 `Control.offset_transform_*` properties are not used for settle. Bars, strokes and dial arcs are filled rectangles or atlas regions on the art-pixel grid, not `draw_line` or `draw_arc` primitives, because 4.7 line drawing has no antialiasing feather. A needle's tip is quantised to whole HUD px, and the Filter's never-rest rule (`NEVER_REST_MAX_S` 1.0 s) must hold at that quantisation. `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` **is set to true on the root only as a bonus if spike S1 shows it exists and takes effect on the HUD `CanvasLayer`; nothing relies on it, and no criterion asserts a HUD-px position through it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the rule had said both "not relied on" and "= true on the root")*: the property is the Pipeline's (K21), is **NOT SOURCEABLE** in the pinned reference, and its scope is `[UNV]` (it may be viewport- or project-scoped and so may not apply to a `CanvasLayer`'s controls at all; it appears nowhere under `docs/engine-reference/godot/`; what is sourced is the 4.7 line no-feather rule, breaking-changes.md:31 and rendering.md:11, and `offset_transform` in ui.md). *Why.* HR-6 and the Pipeline's rule that human-built geometry including the HUD is never rotated at runtime (PR-4 rule 5, which lists the HUD). *Edge notes.* How a needle is produced (a pre-baked frame strip, a snapped sprite, a polygon) is -> ADR candidate A; the observable requirement is only the quantisation and the never-rest proof. Behaviour of `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` when `H != k` and with a fractional canvas is NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike.
196	
197	**HS-10. The surface inventory is closed.** *Rule.* The HUD has exactly the surfaces in the table below. Anything else is a scope breach and a lint failure.
198	
199	| Surface | Anchor | Contents | Source read | Register |
200	|---|---|---|---|---|
201	| `hud_strip` | centre-bottom, sitting on the bottom 5 % safe margin | the **breath dial**: arc with pivot cap, three-cell numeral, mark slot; it shows the ambient O2 while `breath_src` is ROOM, GASP or NONE and the suit O2 (the reserve) while it is RESERVE (HS-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | `perceived(suit.o2)` in ROOM, GASP and NONE; `perceived(suit.reserve)` in RESERVE; `view` rung and `breath_src` | reading |
202	| `hud_suit_panel` | bottom-left, inside the margin | reserve, integrity, warmth, charge + lamp switch; per-reading mark slots; the ship-alarm mark slot (HS-22, HS-25); the **ambient-O2 slot** (a three-digit numeral field in the reserve cell, lit only while the strip shows the reserve, HS-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; notice slot; reserved `own_identity` slot *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | `perceived` x 4 + `suit.alarm`, `view` | reading (glass, needle, numeral, fill) + frame |
203	| `hud_rail` | bottom-right, inside the margin | three tool slots in a four-slot geometry (the fourth cell reserved and empty at MVP, X6), glowstick count, carried glyph, scanner reading slot, device keycaps *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | `view`, `tool_*`, glyph token read, `perceived(SCANNER)` | frame + one reading slot |
204	| `hud_prompt` and `hud_bar` | `world_to_hud(anchor_o)` of the focused subject | plate (keycap + verb), NEEDS_TOOL variant, the linear bar | `focus_view`, `channel_view`, hold state | frame (meta) |
205	| `hud_notice` | at the suit panel's edge | failed-write notice; first-frame ship-log line (after a fallback load or a `DEATH_STUB` restore, HS-46) | `save_status`, boot flag, `restore_reason` (a request) | frame (meta) |
206	| `hud_aim_indicator` *(conditional; exists only while `aim_indicator` is on, default off)* | at a fixed radius around the projected chest point, outside the chest keep-out | one direction mark (HS-52): the Controller's published aim direction (16 steps), nothing about any target, range, light or exposure | the Controller's aim direction | meta (class M), honest, never lie-capable *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
207	| inspect card | layer 2, content by In-World Instruments | HUD supplies the frame, `Theme` and components only | Instruments | frame HUD-owned; reading Instruments' *(designed)* |
208	| reserved anchors | `crew_strip` top-left, `chat` left edge below it, `caption` plate slot, `own_identity` on the panel | nothing drawn at MVP | none | anchor (Vertical Slice B) |
209	
210	**Forbidden surfaces** (lint-banned under any setting or state): minimap, compass, objective, off-screen arrow, crew locator, room name, ship status or loop summary, weight / capacity / inventory / slots-free, health bar, damage number, hit flash, Attention / noise / light / illumination / exposure meter, sanity meter / icon / colour, horror indicator, threat bar, proximity indicator or direction to a Horror, beacon or breach glyph, vignette, screen-edge tint, toast, banner, popup, death screen, score, autosave glyph, "repaired" confirmation, a countdown to an event the HUD names (not the reserve numeral, HS-17), loading spinner, any text in Alarm Red, ring / radial / pie / wipe progress, and a UI cursor in `gameplay` (the cursor, reticle and aim-line bans have exactly one exception, the opt-in, off-by-default accessibility aim indicator of HS-52, user ruling D9 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*). **No HUD surface displays or sonifies the Attention level, tell progress, sanity stage or a Horror's proximity; the chest-lamp state and suit vitals are the player's own, never the web's** (Attention, Adaptive Audio). The HUD contains no horror indicator, threat bar, proximity indicator or direction: a Horror is shown in the world, never by a meter (Horror Entities; Pillar 3). **The HUD draws no beacon or breach glyph under reduce-flashing or any other setting** (Attention C27 and V14: the 'HUD glyph' named by 2D Lighting's LO-26 would be an Attention indicator, which the art bible forbids at ART:741; under reduce-flashing the static world mark and the audio carry the breach). The HS-25 ship-alarm mark is not that glyph and never keys on Attention's phase.
211

content.content:
281	**HS-39. Placement and keep-out.** *Rule.* Placement follows Interaction's AD-5 (cited, not restated): beyond the subject on the line from the player through the anchor, then above, below, right, left. The chest keep-out `PROMPT_KEEPOUT_PX` 16 around the projected chest point is never overlapped, including in the fallback; the fallback offset is `PROMPT_ANCHOR_OFFSET_WORLD_PX` 28 (world px) after AD-5; `PROMPT_EDGE_MARGIN_PX` 4 from the safe margin. If no position satisfies keep-out and margin, the plate is **not drawn** (as off-screen), never clamped over the chest. Plate and bar sizes are HUD px, independent of zoom. The strip, panel and rail rectangles are an exclusion region: a prompt is moved or withheld, never drawn over a reading. *Why.* The chest lamp's beam origin is the chest point; a plate over it would mask the beam. The plate swims against its anchor by at most `H / 2` screen px because plates are integer multiples of `H`; this is the cost of that rule and is not a defect.
282	
283	**HS-40. The channel bar: a linear bar at three length classes.** *Rule.* One linear bar with a needle-mark on the focused plate's long edge facing away from the anchor; never screen-fixed, never a ring or radial. "A linear bar at three sizes" is read as **three length classes keyed to `channel_view.length_class`** — SHORT, MEDIUM, LONG — with interior lengths `BAR_LEN_SHORT_PX` 16 / `BAR_LEN_MEDIUM_PX` 24 / `BAR_LEN_LONG_PX` 40 HUD art px `[PH]` (each 12-64, ordered S < M < L), **not three HUD scales** (HR-13 forbids any HUD scale change). `length_class` is Interaction's derivation (SHORT if HOLD_CONFIRM; MEDIUM if the declared duration is below `BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` 240; else LONG), frozen at the press and never a function of `hp`. Anatomy: a track of outer height 6 (1 border, 4 interior, 1 border) on the plate's own Ground, fill in Tungsten fixture `#FFCC66` as stepped rectangles, a Paper White needle-mark 2 wide by 8 tall overhanging the track by one pixel above and below; `fill_px = floor(progress_pm * L / 1000)`. Fill steps are positional and are not luminance events. The bar stays until the simulation's abort even after the plate hides because `lit` was lost (at most 5 dark ticks). Interaction's Open Question 1 ("a linear bar at three sizes has no repo source") is answered *adopted* and left in Open Questions for the user's confirmation. *Why.* The routed thread and HR-13; the past decision "a linear bar, never a ring".
284	
285	**HS-41. Bar states, mapped to `channel_view.state`.**
286	
287	| `state` | Bar | Plate | Cue source |
288	|---|---|---|---|
289	| IDLE | none | per `focus_view` | none |
290	| ACK (Adapter-local pre-play; never a simulation state, ia:304) | the keycap face drops 1 art px and the track appears at fill 0, from `confirm_view.pressed` (agreed shape, HS-6), on the same render frame as the accepted press, **force-admitting the plate if it was not yet shown** (HS-37); withdrawn within `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS` 2 if no result arrives | stays | the press read |
291	| CONFIRMED (the simulation's confirmation) | keeps the pre-play (or draws the track at fill 0 at once if no ACK was drawn); a CONFIRMED that does not arrive within `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS` withdraws the pre-play | stays | `transition_seq` |
292	| PROGRESS | `fill_px` and the needle-mark at the fill edge; stepped | stays; hides the same frame `prompt_state` goes HIDDEN, while the **bar stays until the simulation's abort** | `progress_pm` |
293	| ABORT | **by `channel_view.ended_by`, never `abort_cause`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the row said "one frame set for every cause", contradicting the cancel drain below, D.16 and AC-HS-65)*: `WORLD` (and `NONE`): the fill snaps empty and a 2 x 2 Ground break-notch is held `BAR_HOLD_DONE_TICKS` 12, then the bar is removed, the same frame set for every world cause; `PLAYER_CANCEL`: the fill drains right to left over `BAR_DRAIN_MS` 400 (D.16; reduced motion snaps to 0), then the bar is removed, with no notch | stays 12 ticks (WORLD) / until the drain ends (PLAYER_CANCEL) | `transition_seq`, `ended_by` |
294	| DONE | full; holds `BAR_HOLD_DONE_TICKS`, then a cut. No checkmark, flash, sparkle or "repaired" text | stays | `result_seq` |
295	| OUTCOME | fills exactly as DONE, then is removed at once; the plate border steps Graphite lit to Graphite mid for 12 ticks; no text says why | dimmed one step | `outcome` |
296	| immediate reject | nothing is drawn; any pre-drawn acknowledgement is withdrawn within one render frame; no shake, flash, red or text, identical for every reason. On a reject the bar is removed and the keycap is **restored and held in the one-step Graphite-lit state for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` 9 `[PH]`** (range 6-18; Interaction V-10 and IA-15, as amended in its design review; this knob is HUD-owned), with **at most one reject presentation per seat per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`**, so a rejected press leaves a perceivable trace on a plate that is shown, while still no shake, flash, red or text and the same frame set for every reason; a rejected press with no plate shown draws nothing (a dip on an unlit subject would be an oracle). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | withdrawn | the result event `kind` REJECTED |
297	
298	Cues are edge-detected from `transition_seq` / `result_seq` per seat (a render frame may span several ticks, so a terminal transition is never skipped; intermediate loops are skipped). Only the **local seat's** `channel_view` is drawn. *Edge notes.* The Controller GDD's phrase that the bar "holds then drains on a world abort" is the older text; this GDD adopts Interaction's snap-plus-notch, the later owner of verbs and visuals, and a refresh is owed to the Controller prose. **The cancel drain.** Interaction specifies a drain for a player cancel (its visual row V-6: "Cancel, hold released ... Bar drains right to left at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE` x fill speed (cosmetic: the sim channel already ended)"; the channel table at ia:336: "the bar snaps empty (cancel drains at the cosmetic drain rate)"; IA-15 lists `CANCELLED` among the closed abort causes; AC-IA-100 expects four visibly different sequences — drain; snap with a 12-tick break-notch; full bar then plate dim; held full bar) **and** says in IA-41 that `abort_cause` is "diagnostic only; the HUD uses one abort frame set for every cause". Those two statements are inconsistent inside Interaction. Resolution: Interaction publishes the non-diagnostic `channel_view.ended_by` (`NONE | PLAYER_CANCEL | WORLD`, registry `ended_by`); the HUD draws the **drain** on `PLAYER_CANCEL` and the **snap with break-notch** on `WORLD`, and never reads `abort_cause`. **The drain is capped and written in integers** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the drain at the earlier `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE` x fill-speed scaled with the channel (a 360-tick weld bar took up to 3 s to empty, and two channels could overlap), so the HUD's cosmetic drain takes `BAR_DRAIN_MS` 400 `[PH]` from any fill and any `length_class` (D.16), and a new ACK snaps any drain in progress to its end before the new bar starts, so drains never stack. (For a hold-to-confirm release the Controller's own `b` drains at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE` over 0.4 s from full, D.10, and the HUD draws `b`; the HUD adds no second drain.) The 400 ms cap shortens Interaction's V-6 cosmetic drain for long channels: a cross-GDD note to Interaction. **The one-tick race (why the Adapter's release read is not used):** a world abort inside tick t's hook can land before the Adapter's `cancel_channel` is applied as `IA_CANCEL_NOOP` at t+1 (ia:741), so a HUD keyed off the Adapter's release would draw a drain for an UNLIT abort; `ended_by` is written with the terminal state, so that abort reads `WORLD`.
299	
300	**HS-42. Hold-to-confirm.** *Rule.* The same bar at SHORT on the focused control's plate, `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` 0.8 by default (48 ticks, 3 ticks per px; the player may adjust the hold, so the fill rate follows the Controller's `hold_pm` and the HUD holds no hold constant); release drains it (the Controller's own `b` drains at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE`, D.10, and the HUD draws it); no Alarm Red, no mark, no dialog. **Two modes (`confirm_view.mode`, HS-6), both required at MVP:** `HOLD` fills the bar over `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`; `TAP` (the Controller's one-handed preset, `confirm_mode` `TAP`, `CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW` 3 s) shows no fill but thickens the bracket and relabels the plate `verb_confirm_prompt` ("Confirm?") while the first tap is armed, and disarms on a focus or context change as the Controller says. The relabel, the bracket thickening and their disarm or expiry restore are **state-display draws of the shared limiter** (HS-47 class A, re-review): the Controller's armed state changes at once, the drawn relabel follows when the limiter admits it and always shows the latest armed state, and the second tap is never gated by what is drawn *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The hold fraction `b` is in neither Interaction simulation view; `focus_view` supplies `mode = HOLD_CONFIRM` and `duration_class = SHORT` (ia:310), which selects the SHORT bar, while the hold fraction and the armed state come from the Controller's Adapter-local `confirm_view` (HS-6; the shape is published at pci:953 and Interaction IA-41, with the `mode` / `armed` fields still to be added, OQ-HS-18). The 0.8 s hold is the core loop's main motor-accessibility barrier, which is why the tap mode is a setting at MVP and not an Alpha accessibility add-on (the two-tap alternative and the adjustable hold are defaults applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80); the Chart Table's menu items use the same component on layer 3 **for the look only** (its Delete hold of 1.6 s, 2 x `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`, is a default applied confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D81: 96 ticks over a 16-px track is 6 ticks per px, inside the 10-tick bound of Game Feel): the Chart Table's destructive-action bar snaps to empty on abort (CT-22); the release drain is the Controller's `b` for a hold (Chart Table C19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Why.* The Controller's UI Requirements and Interaction's statement that the simulation never sees a partial hold. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
301	
302	**HS-43. The carry state and the closed prompt set.** *Rule.* While carrying, the only prompts are `G . Drop` anchored at the foot origin plus the two carry-admitted verbs of Boarding's BS-9: `verb_install` (`install_module`) on a HARDPOINT whose `compatible_defs` lists the carried def, and the pod-console hop plate (`pod_hop` on the CONSOLE); nothing on any other world target. Any reason shown for an unavailable `pod_hop` uses Web Map's WM-9 reason words, and no plate or reason names mass, weight or condition; no carried-weight number, inventory or value tag is drawn (HS-32). The carried-module glyph and drop keycap are on the rail (HS-32). The thrown glowstick in flight is a cosmetic Adapter-side arc (Interaction's Open Question 7); the HUD draws nothing for it and the rail count steps on acceptance. *Why.* Boarding & Salvage's closed carry-prompt set and Assembly's "the prompt may be late, never wrong".

input.old_string: *Why.* The Controller's UI Requirements and Interaction's statement that the simulation never sees a partial hold. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
input.new_string:
*Why.* The Controller's UI Requirements and Interaction's statement that the simulation never sees a partial hold. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**(b) The give_up confirm plate** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; user ruling D7; CD ruling on PCI re-review)*. A DOWNED player has no focused object, so the HUD owns one DOWNED-only plate (surface `hud_give_up_plate`, HS-10) for the solo "give up and reload" action (user ruling D7; the Controller's PC-2 and UI Requirements 1). **Trigger:** `confirm_view.give_up_live` (HS-6) only; the HUD reads no `loco_state` and no Co-op state (the Controller folds DOWNED, solo, context `gameplay` and Co-op Session's revive gate, R9: undesigned, provisional, constant false at MVP, into the one bool). **Show:** on the first render frame it is true, with the track at fill 0 and no press needed (the exit is discoverable), without the prompt show-debounce; re-shows are spaced by EC-HS-57. **Contents:** one keycap from `glyph_view(seat, give_up)` (HOLD variant in HOLD mode, two-pip variant in TAP mode, as HS-37), the verb text from string key `plate_give_up` (English placeholder "Give up", `tr()`, instrument face), and the SHORT linear bar with needle-mark: `fill_px = (hold_pm * BAR_LEN_SHORT_PX) div 1000` with `BAR_LEN_SHORT_PX` 16 (0.8 s hold = 48 ticks = 3 ticks per px, as above); the HUD does no drain of its own (the Controller drains `hold_pm` at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE` 2.0). A press (`confirm_view.pressed_action == give_up`) drops the keycap 1 art px (ACK, HS-41); in TAP mode the bracket thickens and the plate relabels `verb_confirm_prompt` while armed (class A state display, HS-47). **Hide:** on the first render frame `give_up_live` is false (recovery, DEAD, or a revive-capable seat in VS-B), with the bar zeroed; never drawn in any other state. It is not suppressed by `TRANSIT_HOLD` (statuses run in the pod and a DOWNED in the pod is the Controller's, D60), freezes undimmed under `PAUSED_FROZEN` like any plate, and after a restore into DOWNED it is drawn at fill 0 on the first `RUNNING` frame. **Co-existence:** while DOWNED the object prompt (HS-37) is not drawn (the Controller ignores `interact` in DOWNED), so at most one plate exists; the plate reuses the prompt-plate and bar components, adds one node and no new asset beyond the existing keycap variants. **Placement:** HS-39 (outside the chest keep-out, never withheld). **Wording:** verb text only, no cause, count, countdown, consequence or death word (X8; `HUD_DEATH_WORDS` lint, Tone and language); no Alarm Red, no mark. Truth, meta register, never lie-capable; no sound requested by the HUD. A result event REJECTED for `give_up` (for example the race with a revive) draws nothing: the plate is already gone. The plate depends on no world state (no lit, exposure, Attention or Horror read), so it cannot be an oracle (P3).

314
**HS-47. The flash arbiter (`hud_flash_budget`).** *Rule.* One arbiter counts luminance events per rolling second across the HUD. **Its clock is the committed tick `T`** (window `(T - TICK_RATE, T]`): `present_time` drives animation, not the budget; an event that originates in render time (a focus becoming stable, a press) is stamped with the tick current at that render frame, and while the kernel is `PAUSED` `T` does not advance, so no deferrable event is admitted while paused. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The event inventory** (every HUD luminance event, with its class; the events added by the review are marked *new*): **clock-locked, never delayed:** mark leading edges (at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0`); honest-numeral **grid boundaries** at `T mod HONEST_GRID_TICKS == 0` at which at least one displayed digit actually changes (a boundary with no displayed change is not an event, so the 2 events/s is a ceiling reached only while the numerals are falling), which are **skip-only**: drawn on their own tick or skipped, never delayed. **Never rescheduled by the HUD:** lying-digit ticks (the Filter's schedule). **Follow the honest source state, counted, never deferred:** source-state hue cuts (HSV-4, L-5: a glyph or arc band changing between its loop hue and Graphite lit). **Source-state swap** *(new, re-review)*: the strip's `breath_src` swap (HS-12, HSV-42), counted once, never deferred, like a hue cut. **Orphan transitions** *(new, re-review)*: a plate hide whose show-start lies before the window, and a mark OFF edge whose ON edge does, are counted once in `N(w)` for the windows that contain them (they are known only when they occur, so they are non-deferrable and may overrun, D.2). **A counted mark event is an actual change in the drawn luminance of a mark slot, not a scheduled boundary** *(new, re-review)*: three cases were missing from the inventory. (1) A **leading edge** at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` counts only when the slot is active and w
as drawn OFF (outline to fill); at a tick where the mark is already drawn ON (held solid by STRICT or reduced motion, held by pause, or bridged after a resume, HS-23) the natural edge changes nothing and is **not** counted. (2) A **mid-phase appearance**: an inactive slot becoming active draws the filled square at once when it is solid (STRICT, reduced motion) or when the live phase is inside the duty (D.4), which is one counted, non-deferrable event at that tick; in the pulsing case outside the duty it draws the OFF outline (a luminance change, one event) and the next leading edge is then counted normally. (3) The **pause-induced edge** (entering the hold from an OFF phase) is one event, per HS-23. The scheduled mark entry in `W(t)` is conditional: it exists only for a slot that is active **and** pulsing (not solid, not paused), so a solid mark reserves no capacity. **Input-driven, two classes** *(re-review: the earlier single class, "counted, never deferred", let spam raise the HUD above the ceiling and is replaced)*: **(A) State displays**, whose *simulation state changes at once and is never delayed* but whose *drawn state* goes through **one shared coalescing limiter** for the whole class: the tool-switch bracket and Tungsten move (HSV-13), the glowstick count substitution (HSV-15; the suppressant's, HSV-14, is dormant until the tool returns), the lamp-switch glyph (HS-19, HSV-12), and the TAP-mode "Confirm?" relabel and its disarm or expiry restore (HS-42, *new to the inventory*). The limiter admits at most one state-display draw per `GLYPH_STATE_LATCH_TICKS` 20 across the **whole class** (so at most 3 per rolling second from the class, not 3 per kind), each admitted draw shows the **latest** simulation state (intermediate states are never drawn, the count and the bracket jump straight to the current value), and each admitted draw is also a deferrable event through `admit` (so it yields to prompts and the grid and never lands in a full window); a pending draw 
that has waited `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60 is force-admitted and counted (overrun, recorded). The final drawn state therefore equals the simulation state within `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` ticks of the last change (AC-HS-140). **(B) Acknowledgement cues**, which cannot be deferred without a press feeling unreceived (Game Feel step 2, the same render frame as the accepted press): the force-admitted show-start of an accepted press and the ACK keycap dip (one event, they land on the same frame, HS-37, HSV-24), the reject keycap hold (HS-41), and the OUTCOME plate-border step (HSV-29), which follows the simulation's result. They are counted and never deferred, **rate-gated by their own gates** (at most one ACK-plus-force-admit and at most one reject presentation per seat per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`; one OUTCOME step per channel), and **may overrun a full window**: an overrun is recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` and nothing is dropped. **Deferrable:** prompt show-starts with no press; the scanner reading's show-start (HSV-34, *new*); the notice and first-frame-line show-starts; and the state-display class (A) as above (lowest priority). Positional changes (bar fill, needle motion, arc settle, charge-fill steps) are not luminance events. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Two counting modes (user rulings D91 (iv) and D79)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `flash_mode` is STRICT while `reduce_flashing` is on (its first-launch default) and WEIGHTED otherwise. STRICT counts every event of the inventory above, as before. WEIGHTED weights a flash by the area it changes (WCAG 2.3.1; the registry's `flash_count` takes a region as a ninth of the displayed picture) and exempts exactly two classes, **honest-numeral digit swaps (grid boundaries) and prompt show-starts**, when the event's `flash_weight_pm` is below `FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM` (D.2). An exempt event is neither counted nor deferred, so a prompt waits for its debounce alone; the grid stays clock-locked and skip-only in both 
modes because it is a shared cadence, not a budget decision. **The Alarm Red mark's edges are always counted strictly, in both modes** (a red flash is held to the strict ceiling; `flash_count` includes red flash). Every other event of the inventory (source-state hue cuts, input-driven small-area events, notice, scanner and lamp-glyph changes) stays counted in both modes. Lying-digit ticks are the Filter's schedule and are counted in both modes until the Filter adopts the same weighting (note to the Perception Filter). A deferrable event is admitted at tick `t` only if the count in the half-open window `(t - TICK_RATE, t]` plus itself plus the clock-locked events already scheduled in that window stays at or below `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`; otherwise it waits. The normative admission test is the Formulas entry D.2 (`hud_flash_budget`), which also checks every forward window ending at an already-scheduled clock-locked event in `(t, t + TICK_RATE)`; this sentence is its summary. Hide events are never deferred. **Priority order (HUD-owned; it never touches the Filter's scheduler; in WEIGHTED mode the exempt classes leave the order and it governs what remains):** hides are never deferred; mark edges are never deferred; Filter lying-digit ticks are never rescheduled; among the HUD-owned deferrable events (the grid boundary is skip-only, never delayed) the order is prompt show-start, then the honest grid boundary, then notice or scanner show-start, then the state-display class (the lamp-switch glyph, the bracket, the count, the TAP relabel). **Grid-skip rule, with its bounds** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a grid boundary that would exceed the budget while a prompt show-start waits is skipped, and the next boundary shows the then-latest value; **a boundary is never skipped twice in a row** (`GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS` 1, a rule constant, not a knob): the boundary after a skip is admitted and counted whatever waits, so **numeral lag is bounded by `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` uncondition
ally**. A waiting prompt then waits **at most one grid cell when at most one other counted event is in the window** (the case of the breach example), and otherwise at most **`MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60** `[PH]` ticks (range 30-120; one full window), after which it is force-admitted and counted as an overrun, so every deferrable event (prompt, notice, scanner, state display) has a stated worst-case wait and none can starve; the previous claim "a prompt waits at most one grid cell" held only with at most one other counted event, because nothing limited consecutive skips, and is restated with its precondition. The scanner reading's `SCAN_READING_DWELL_S` starts at its **admission**, not at the scan result, so a deferred show-start cannot eat the dwell (the reference breach scenario in Game Feel confirms the order: AC-HS-127; the bound cases are AC-HS-140 and AC-HS-141). The inspect card's honest numeral (In-World Instruments) shares the same grid boundary and adds no event; the card's lying digits are Filter-scheduled, counted and never delayed. Positional changes (bar fill steps, needle motion, arc settle) are not luminance events. If the arithmetic shows that the sum can exceed `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` with every HUD-owned event at its floor — which it can at Vertical Slice A when a lying digit's schedule (3.0 transitions/s at `N_r` 2 or more) already fills the ceiling — that is an **ASK to the Filter and the accessibility-specialist**, never a HUD override; the HUD records `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` and does not change the Filter's schedule. *Why.* The Filter owns the tick scheduler; the HUD owns only its own events. **The counting unit is ruled (user, D91 (ii))** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a flash is one pair of opposing transitions and a window's flash count is `ceil(n_transitions / 2)` (registry `flash_count`). The arbiter counts *leading-edge events* (mark cycle, grid boundary, show-start, substitution), and D.2 shows that this count bounds `ceil(n / 2)` from above
, so staying at or below `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` events keeps the ruled count at or below it; under it the mark is 0.47/s and the honest grid 2/s. The edge unit (each edge of a cycle counted) is retired. The literal `ceil(n / 2)` would admit more single transitions per second; the HUD does not use that headroom, because it would unpin the grid proof of HS-14 and the Filter counts its own ticks separately. *Edge notes.* Unreachable at MVP (lies are dormant), but the honest-numeral grid already depends on the unit.

content.content:
== 326
**HS-53. Pause, DOWNED, DEAD, restore and transit.** *Rule.* The full state table is in States and Transitions. In brief: solo pause freezes the HUD undimmed, with one exception: an active mark is held ON solid (HS-23); DOWNED keeps the readings updating and the lamp lit with marks persisting; DEAD freezes the readings with no death screen, score or text; the first `RUNNING` frame after a restore draws the readings at restored values with no settle, no abort frame, no notch, clears every presentation-local counter (debounce, hold grid, bar fill, tick phases, flash history), and reads `restore_reason` only as a request, never altering hallucination content from `DEATH_STUB` (it keys only the one record line of HS-46); `TRANSIT_HOLD` and the pod leg leave the HUD's layout unchanged while statuses run in the pod (user ruling D60): the readings keep updating from `perceived` as in `RUNNING` and stay lie-capable, and a death in the pod is the Controller's `DEAD` (the DEAD state below). **Who owns the visible step from death to restore, and what it is** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; Save/Load SL-7)*: **Save/Load owns it, and it is automatic.** At the tick boundary where the seat becomes `DEAD`, Save/Load settles or abandons the in-flight write, picks a generation (SL-8) and calls `request_restore` with `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB`; the kernel enters `LOADING` (the command queue is flushed); the Pipeline shows layer-1 black (`TRANSIT_HOLD`) while the HUD stays unchanged, holding its last model; the first `RUNNING` frame is the `RESTORE_FRAME` below, with the camera cut at the pre-load zoom step. **The player presses nothing, and there is no designed dwell** (no death screen, no dim-out, no sound, SL-7), so the HUD's DEAD state lasts only until the restore completes; if no candidate loads (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`) the Chart Table shows a boot-flow screen (Save/Load OQ-42). The cryo re-wake sequence is Failure Contract & Re-wake's at Vertical Slice A. The HUD adds nothing to this step beyond the one record line on the first `RUNNING` frame (HS-46); AC-HS-132 and AC-HS-136 assert the HUD's side of it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Whether the player understands why the game restarted** (P5 depends on it; the one peripheral line after a hard cut may read as a crash) is a **measured playtest question, OQ-HS-84** (pass bar: 7 of 8 testers can say why); the ruling is not re-opened, and any fix is owned by the world or by Save/Load, never by HUD
 text *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Why.* P5 and the user decision that MVP death restarts from the last autosave (owned by Save/Load).
== 332
**HS-56. Non-Ground area at rest.** *Rule.* At rest (all readings OK, no prompt, no mark, no notice) the number of HUD-layer pixels that are neither Ground `#1C2128` nor transparent, captured with the world hidden and the root clear colour set to a sentinel, is at most `HUD_NONGROUND_PX_MAX` = 1 % of the 640 x 360 HUD canvas = 2,304 HUD px `[PH]` (range 1.0-1.5 %): `nonground_count`. This is the measurable form of the art bible's "about 1 %, tunable". It is a screenshot-diff criterion (manual, with a retained screenshot). *Why.* P1: the world, not the HUD, is the picture. The art-director's first allocation (strip about 300, panel about 875, rail about 885, headroom 184 of 2,304) is an estimate the UX spec re-measures. The 1-HUD-px letterbox hairline the Pipeline suggests is **declined for the HUD layer** (a 640 x 360 perimeter hairline is 1,996 px, 87 % of the budget); if the Pipeline wants one it is drawn on layer 1 and excluded from the count.
== 334
**HS-57. Neighbour boundaries.** *Rule.* **Inspect card:** layer 2, frame and components HUD-owned; content, context and card-gauge parity (the card reads the same `perceived` ref as the wall gauge and lies exactly when it lies) are In-World Instruments' *(designed)*. Instruments accepts this division (iw:508, iw:529), adopts `HONEST_TICK_MS` for the card numeral and requests its flash slots from `hud_flash_budget` (iw:264), confirms HS-33 (the field-check reading is the HUD's, iw K-9), registers `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` as its own constant at 16 unchanged (iw:1706, iw:1076; registry entry `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX`, source Instruments), places the card outside the at-rest non-Ground count (iw:327), and asks the HUD to repeat three clauses, which this GDD repeats here and in Acceptance Criteria: the HUD draws **no sanity surface**; the HUD **may not read `node()` or `edge()`**; and HS-56's non-Ground cap is measured **at rest only** (no prompt, mark, notice or card). **Debug Overlay:** layer 4, a `DIAGNOSTIC` subscriber, dev builds only, never an accessibility feature *(designed)*; its P-1 (do:423, do:783) asks the HUD's Acceptance Criteria to repeat "no `true_value` call site" (AC-PF-51) and "no Overlay control in any HUD state", and no HUD node hosts, instantiates or parents an Overlay node. The HUD exposes a read-only `hud_debug_snapshot()`; it carries **no `k`**, because no HUD code reads `k` (HS-2) and the Overlay reads `k` from the Pipeline. The Overlay consumes the snapshot as a read-only channel (do:417, do:777): it carries `H`, the picture rect, the plate rectangles, the mark phase, the last model and the nine AC-HS-122 counters, with no `k`; the HUD exposes no other overlay hooks. **Onboarding:** no tutorial overlay, hint or tooltip at MVP; a future first-use prompt uses the existing plate *(provisional — Onboarding undesigned)*. **Chart Table:** layer 3; in solo pause the HUD stays visible and frozen behind it. *Why.* Reflexion patterns 1 and 11.
